snapshot.text: Three-part system of public hospitals, union-run social insurance funds (obras sociales) and private prepaid plans. The Milei government has cut and merged health bodies, confirmed the exit from WHO (Argentina still takes part in PAHO) and presents health as a driver of private investment.

priorities.title: Health system reform and WHO exit
priorities.text: A reform package of the health system, with the withdrawal from WHO confirmed and a review of vaccines and medicines; Argentina did take part in PAHO's 63rd Directing Council.

priorities.title: Health as an investment sector
priorities.text: Minister Lugones says health is already a driver of Argentine development and that the state should create conditions for private investment.

priorities.title: Under pressure: fentanyl and PAMI
priorities.text: The minister faces pressure over the contaminated fentanyl case and the crisis at PAMI, the pensioners' health insurer; an impeachment request was filed in the Chamber of Deputies.

netherlands.text: The Netherlands is Argentina's third-largest investor; science cooperation covers human and animal health. No bilateral health programme with the Milei government found.

timeline.text: At Argentina Week in New York, Lugones pitches the health sector to investors.
Minister calls health 'a driver of Argentine development'.
Ministry reports savings of ARS 116 billion and new hospital measures.
Argentina takes part in PAHO's 63rd Directing Council; new map of active doctors published.
